subject: test-planner
reason: Split by observable behaviour on the checkout page: one e2e case each for the renamed Address message, the renamed Zip code message, the unchanged City/State/Country messages, the validation summary, no order on invalid submit, per-field messages with only some fields empty, and a successful order with every field filled.

excluded.reason: No API, Basket, Ordering or domain change; the WebApp has no unit test project and the messages exist only in the rendered page

excluded.item: Payment fields and the 'Your cart is empty' message
Exact wording beyond the story's 'for example' messages
excluded.reason: Ambiguous; the most literal reading is asserted and the ambiguity is recorded under Open questions

items.title: Empty Address shows "The Address field is required." under Address
items.reason: This is the core defect: the message under the Address input named the hidden property "Street". It is its own case so a regression in the Address rename fails independently of Zip code. Only the rendered checkout page shows the message, so it runs on e2e.

items.title: Empty Zip code shows "The Zip code field is required." under Zip code
covers: Expected: message under Zip code names "Zip code"
items.reason: The second half of the defect: the Zip code message named the property "ZipCode". A separate case so a missing or misspelled display name for this field (for example "Zipcode") is reported on its own. The message only exists in the rendered page, hence e2e.

items.title: Empty City, State and Country keep their unchanged required messages
covers: Expected: messages for City, State and Country are unchanged
items.reason: The story requires the other three messages to stay as they were; a fix that renamed or removed them (for example a blanket display-name change or custom message) would break this. One case covers the three because they share one unchanged-behaviour requirement. e2e because the messages are rendered by the page.

items.title: The validation summary next to Place order lists the five messages with the visible names
covers: Expected: the list of messages next to Place order uses the same names
Actual: the list next to the button repeats both names
items.reason: The bug report says the summary list repeated "Street" and "ZipCode"; the summary is rendered separately from the per-field messages (`ValidationSummary`), so it needs its own assertion. e2e because only the page renders it.

items.title: Submitting with every address field empty places no order
covers: Algorithm: HandleSubmitAsync submits only when validation passes
items.reason: The story keeps "no order is placed" for empty fields; adding display names must not change whether validation blocks submission. A separate case because it asserts persisted state (no order, basket kept), not message text. e2e because the order flow runs through the WebApp, Basket and Ordering on the test stack.

items.title: Only the empty fields show a message when Address and Zip code alone are cleared
covers: Expected: every empty field shows that it is required
Expected: message under Zip code names "Zip code"
items.reason: "Every empty field shows that it is required" implies filled fields show nothing; this checks the renamed messages appear per field and in the summary without the other fields' messages, which the all-empty cases cannot distinguish. e2e because the messages are rendered by the page.

items.title: With every address field filled, Place order places the order
covers: Expected: with every field filled in, the order is placed as today
Implementation Notes: property names Street and ZipCode stay for the order flow
items.reason: The fix touches the form model the order is built from; the story requires checkout to still succeed. A regression (for example renaming the properties instead of adding display names) would break the payload to Basket/Ordering. Creating an order needs the full test stack, so e2e.

items.reason: The spec calls demo.caption('After Place order: <url>') after the click, but no keyframe shows that caption (06-step and 07-highlight show the My orders page with no caption, while the 'Opened ...' captions do render). The redirect to /user/orders is asserted with toHaveURL but appears in the recording only through the 'My orders' heading (lesson L2). The same caption is also missing from the post-submit frames of TC-01/02/05, where the Checkout heading and form identify the page.

The expected result 'No validation message and no validation summary item is shown' is asserted with .validation-message and ul.validation-errors li counts of 0 only after toHaveURL(/user/orders), where checkout messages cannot exist, so it cannot fail. The requirement is still proven indirectly by the redirect and the placed order; asserting the counts right after the click, before waiting for the URL, would make it meaningful.
